## Austin Community Tech Meetup: 4-Hour Evening Flow

A balanced evening for students and job seekers works best when it starts with energy, adds practical value early, and ends with interaction. This schedule fits all required sessions into **18:00–22:00 America/Chicago** with one **10-minute break**.

## Engaging Session Sequence for 2026-08-14

| Time | Session | Duration | Why it fits here |
|---|---|---:|---|
| 18:00–18:15 | Sponsor intro | 15 min | Quick welcome, housekeeping, and event support |
| 18:15–18:35 | Lightning talk on AI tools | 20 min | Fast, high-interest opener to hook the room |
| 18:35–19:20 | Workshop on résumé writing | 45 min | Practical early-session value for job seekers |
| 19:20–19:30 | Break | 10 min | Reset, refill, and informal mingling |
| 19:30–20:20 | Panel on career switches | 50 min | Broader discussion with relatable stories and advice |
| 20:20–20:50 | Networking block | 30 min | Let attendees connect while ideas are fresh |
| 20:50–21:30 | Q&A | 40 min | Open floor for follow-up questions and deeper discussion |
| 21:30–22:00 | Open mingle / wrap-up buffer | 30 min | Comfortable close, final conversations, and exit time |

## Schedule Rationale for a Mixed Audience

- **Starts with momentum:** the sponsor intro is short, then the AI talk gives everyone a quick win.
- **Practical before abstract:** résumé writing comes before the panel so attendees can immediately apply ideas.
- **Social energy mid-evening:** networking lands after the panel, when people have shared topics to talk about.
- **Strong closing:** Q&A gives the audience direct access to speakers, and the final buffer keeps the event from feeling rushed.

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Add to calendar](https://calendar.google.com/)
Action: [Button: Build agenda](https://www.notion.so/)

## Sources

- Austin time zone reference: https://www.timeanddate.com/time/zones/cdt
- General event scheduling reference: https://www.eventbrite.com/blog/event-timeline/
